key_insight: Forward CIP (F-CIP) turns controllable information production into a reward signal derived only from system dynamics, enabling unsupervised RL to discover useful behaviors without hand-designed intrinsic rewards.
engineering_relevance: This reduces reward-engineering effort for new robots and tasks, while still producing primitive skills that can be combined with simple task rewards to learn coordinated locomotion.
method: Reformulate Controllable Information Production as an RL-native objective called Forward CIP.
Use the environment’s dynamics directly, avoiding the need to choose information variables by hand.
Pair F-CIP with existing RL algorithms to learn intrinsic behaviors such as balancing and controllability.
evidence_signal: The paper reports that agents trained with F-CIP discovered primitive behaviors like balancing and, when combined with a simple forward-velocity reward, learned coordinated gaits such as hopping and running.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality and compatibility of the environment dynamics with the F-CIP objective, so results may vary across tasks and implementations.
paper_title: Bellman Meets Lyapunov: Unsupervised Reinforcement Learning via Mastering Chaos
